first_impression.summary_in_own_words: It's a guide to getting married in Portugal, sorted by region, with the legal stuff for Aussie passports, and a person called a Wedded Advisor I can talk to. 'Get Married in Portugal, from a Sintra Palace to an Algarve Cliff' sounds pretty. The quick answer that we can legally marry there with a month's notice, or do a symbolic one and sign at home, is exactly the 'where do I start' bit I need. There's no price up top, but they've told me there are no packages, so I'm not expecting one there.

attention_map.quote: Wedded Concierge plans weddings in Portugal for couples from Australia, the United States and the United Kingdom, with one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend
attention_map.why: Australia is named and they say one person handles it from start to finish. That's what I want, because I can't deal with suppliers across time zones. The legal quick answer is calming. But 'one Wedded Advisor' is a job title. I still don't know who that actually is.

attention_map.quote: Which season are you planning for? ... How many guests? ... 'Check your date'
attention_map.why: Three taps and no long form, so I'd use it on my phone at 10pm. But it's me telling them my guest count. The page doesn't tell me whether Portugal works for 60 people.

attention_map.quote: a non-numeric line naming Wedded Concierge and one Wedded Advisor, or hide the strip
attention_map.why: If it's just the brand name again, I scroll straight past. It isn't proof of anything.

attention_map.quote: a ceremony in a Sintra national palace or park booked through Parques de Sintra, then a Douro day for guests
attention_map.why: This is the 'something different, not a standard package' feeling I want. A palace you can actually book is a real thing, not just a pretty word. I'd screenshot this and send it to my partner.

attention_map.quote: Guests line: no sourced guest range exists. Leave it out of the cards (or 'Ask your Wedded Advisor')
attention_map.why: The airport codes and setting lines are handy. But the one thing I most need on each card is whether it fits our numbers, and the answer is 'ask'. Every region is the same on that. There's no drive time from the airport for Comporta, and none for the Douro either.

attention_map.quote: Queluz and the National Palace of Sintra can be needed for state events, and events on those dates may have to be cancelled
attention_map.why: Honest, and nobody else tells you this. The scaffolding note on Monserrate until early 2027 makes me trust them more. It's a little scary for a palace wedding though.

attention_map.quote: visa-free short stays on Australian, US and UK passports ... four arrival airports (LIS, OPO, FAO, FNC)
attention_map.why: Good to know our guests won't need visas. The rest overlaps with what I've already read.

attention_map.quote: Exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms; a buy-out is often separate from the venue fee; fees may be per day or per guest with a minimum
attention_map.why: This is the blow-out I'm scared of, and at least they're warning me where it hides. But it tells me how it can go wrong and gives no numbers, so it adds worry without helping me budget.

attention_map.quote: The Australian Embassy in Lisbon can issue a CNI; DFAT also issues CNIs in Australia ... an overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia but in most cases is recognised
attention_map.why: This is the bit for us specifically. I'd save it. The US and UK passport tabs are just clutter on my phone, as long as they really are separate tabs.

attention_map.quote: Fallback until then: explain what drives cost (guest count, region, season, nights at the venue, exclusivity) with no figures, and offer a Wedded Advisor estimate
attention_map.why: This is the deal breaker. If the sign-off doesn't come through, the Costs tab is a list of things that affect cost and still no number. Even if the table does go live, it's in euros, it's for about 100 guests (we're more like 60), and it says 'No Wedded Wonderland figure and no From AUD price on this page'.

attention_map.quote: Venue nights with rooms, welcome dinner, ceremony, long dinner, late party, Sunday brunch, an on-the-day coordinator
attention_map.why: I can picture this, and it feels like us. Being told straight that there's no package and it's a planned weekend instead is fair enough. But it's a list of what a weekend 'can include' with nothing on what it costs.

attention_map.quote: Quinta rooms first, then nearby hotels ... Transfers from Lisbon or Porto
attention_map.why: This answers where our guests stay and how they get there, at least roughly. There are no flight times though, and from Australia that's the first thing our parents will ask.

attention_map.quote: hidden at launch: only 2 Portugal real weddings
attention_map.why: I won't see it, but I'll notice there are no real couples here. That makes it feel like they haven't done many in Portugal.

attention_map.quote: a Wedded Advisor explains fees in your currency on the first call
attention_map.why: So I have to get on a call to find out what they charge. There's no name or face, just 'B14 advisor band' and the founder quote taken out. This is supposed to be the who-plans-it section and it's the thinnest part of the page.

attention_map.quote: Is a wedding in Portugal cheaper than at home?
attention_map.why: I'd tap this one first. If the answer has no comparison and no number, I'll feel dodged.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Celebrity gossip links at the bottom of a planning page. I'd stop scrolling here.

questions_answered.question: What does this cost all in, and what is included in the from price?
questions_answered.evidence: No 'From AUD' price anywhere: 'No Wedded Wonderland figure and no From AUD price on this page'. The only cost table is euros for about 100 guests, and it waits on sign-off. The fallback is cost drivers 'with no figures'. The weekend list (s6) says what 'can' be included, not what a price covers.

questions_answered.question: Can it fit our guest count?
questions_answered.evidence: Region cards carry no guest line ('Ask your Wedded Advisor'). There are no named venues with capacities. The guest count only shows up as a question they ask me in the B9 bar and the form.

questions_answered.question: Who would actually plan this with us, and what do they do?
questions_answered.evidence: 'one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend' plus a How it works block. But there's no named person, no photo, the founder quote is removed, and no approved line on what happens if something goes wrong.

questions_answered.question: How do our guests get there and where do they stay?
questions_answered.evidence: Arrival airports LIS, OPO, FAO, FNC; visa-free for Australians (90 in 180); 'Quinta rooms first, then nearby hotels'; transfers from Lisbon or Porto. No flight times, no drive times except a hedged Lisbon line, no hotel names.

questions_answered.question: Is our budget realistic for this place?
questions_answered.evidence: Best case is EUR 25,000 to 70,000 for about 100 guests, only after sign-off. Nothing for 30 to 80 guests and nothing in AUD. Otherwise it's 'offer a Wedded Advisor estimate'. I can't check my AUD 30,000 to 75,000 against anything without enquiring.

objections_triggered.objection: Prices look like they start low and will blow out
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'Exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms; a buy-out is often separate from the venue fee; fees may be per day or per guest with a minimum' with no figures alongside

objections_triggered.objection: I don't know if my budget is possible for this many people
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Region cards with no guest line, and a cost band only for about 100 guests in euros (or no figures at all in the fallback)

objections_triggered.objection: Planning from overseas, time zones and suppliers I can't meet
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Partly calmed by 'one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend', but there's no name and fees only come up 'on the first call'

objections_triggered.objection: Every planner's page looks the same
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Mostly avoided by the palace rules strip and the passport-specific legal steps; it comes back with the faceless advisor section and hidden real weddings

trust_signals_noticed: Legal steps specific to an Australian passport, with the Embassy and DFAT named
'Legal and cost details checked October 2026, with sources named in each tab'
Honest catches: state-event cancellations, Monserrate scaffolding to Q1 2027
Straight answer that there is no package, a planned weekend instead
Nearest airport code on every region card
turn_offs_noticed: No price signal at all, likely in the fallback version: no From AUD price, and the cost table may show no figures
No guest numbers per region or per venue
Celebrity trending links at the bottom
Very long page (2,400 to 3,200 words) to skim on a phone at night, with lots of US and UK passport detail I don't need

emotional_response.felt: Reassured on the legal side and excited by the Sintra and Douro bits, then deflated when I hit costs and guest numbers.
emotional_response.stress_level: Lower about paperwork, the same about money.
emotional_response.feels_like_us: The weekend description does. The rest reads like a very thorough guide rather than someone planning with us.

payload.decision_reason: Not enough to enquire. There's no from price with inclusions, nothing on whether a region fits our guest count, and no named person, which are the three things I need first. But the Australian legal steps, the honest palace catches and the weekend description are useful and feel different enough to save and send to my partner. I won't enquire until I can tell whether our budget and about 60 guests even work in Portugal.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Okay, this is actually helpful on the 'can we even legally do this' bit, and I love the Sintra palace idea. Saving it for the weekend. But I scrolled the whole thing and I still have no idea what it costs for 60 people in dollars, or whether any of these places hold 60. And who is the advisor? It just says 'a Wedded Advisor'. I'm not filling in a form just to find out if we can afford it.
